closingKeywordReason: Checks 0, 3 and 4b now compare with the latest release tag rather than origin HEAD, so commits to main between releases no longer fire the siren; covered red-first.
assumptions: CONFIRM chosen by the human: alert on releases, not commits; README install pins the marketplace to #latest so installs are releases and the version names the code.

Reference is the floating `latest` tag that release.yml moves to the highest stable vX.Y.Z (#1427/#1481), read with one capped ls-remote of refs/tags/latest* and refs/tags/v*. The pattern is `latest*` because an exact `refs/tags/latest` pattern omits the peeled `latest^{}` line, which would compare the tag object instead of the commit (caught by the fixture).
Check 4b compares the installed version with the release version numerically (X.Y.Z). Same-version commits after a release are not reported; every release bumps plugin.json.
Default taken: a clone ahead of the release (tracking main, or with local commits) is current. A clone with local commits on top of the release is therefore no longer flagged; diverged still is.

Default taken: a detached-HEAD clone (added with #latest) gets `claude plugin marketplace update bop-clocktower`; a clone on a branch keeps `git -C <clone> pull --ff-only`, which the verbatim-remedy test still runs.
The hook stays bash 3.2 compatible (syntax-checked with /bin/bash 3.2.57).
